items.issue: The .reloadtrigger file only gates DevTools when spring.devtools.restart.trigger-file is set, and that property is set nowhere (application-local.yml, application.yml, pom.xml, backend.compose.yml/dev.compose.yml all lack it), so DevTools restarts on any change under target/classes and the 'only reload on a successful compile' guard at lines 35-37 has no effect
items.fix: Add spring.devtools.restart.trigger-file: .reloadtrigger to src/main/resources/application-local.yml (or pass -Dspring-boot.run.jvmArguments=-Dspring.devtools.restart.trigger-file=.reloadtrigger on line 45) so DevTools restarts only when the script touches the trigger

items.issue: The DevTools trigger-file mechanism the header comment describes is inert: 'spring.devtools.restart.trigger-file' is not set anywhere in the repo (grep finds devtools only in pom.xml), so DevTools restarts on the first .class the background 'mvn compile' writes rather than on 'touch target/classes/.reloadtrigger' — meaning a restart can fire mid-compile against a half-written target/classes, and the trigger touch then causes a second, redundant restart per edit.
items.fix: Add 'spring.devtools.restart.trigger-file: .reloadtrigger' under 'spring.devtools.restart' in src/main/resources/application-local.yml (or pass it via -Dspring-boot.run.jvmArguments) so DevTools only restarts when the trigger file is touched after a successful compile.

items.issue: '-Dspring-boot.run.profiles=local' is hard-coded; the spring-boot-maven-plugin turns it into a '--spring.profiles.active=local' command-line argument, which is the highest-precedence property source and therefore silently overrides the SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE env var that compose.yml (line 59) and the workspace run-stack set — so an operator adding a profile (e.g. SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local,debug) gets it ignored with no warning.
items.fix: Honour the environment: 'exec mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles="${SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE:-local}"', or drop the flag entirely and rely on SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE which compose.yml already sets.

items.issue: The hot-reload compile runs offline ('mvn -o') while the foreground 'mvn spring-boot:run' (line 45) runs online — an inconsistency with a concrete failure mode: 'dependency:go-offline' (Dockerfile line 75) is well known to miss plugin artefacts, so if anything needed by the process-classes lifecycle was not pre-fetched, every recompile fails offline, the guarded 'if' swallows it, the trigger is never touched, and hot reload is permanently and silently dead while the container stays healthy.
items.fix: Drop '-o' so the watcher can fetch anything go-offline missed (the container already has network for spring-boot:run), and surface a failure explicitly, e.g. 'mvn -q compile || echo "dev-run: recompile failed" >&2'.

items.issue: The 'locked' contract's whole payload surface contradicts the shipped API: it declares snake_case wire names (address_line_1, town, county, postcode, country, telephone, trace_id, page_size) plus fields that do not exist at all (operator_type, status ACTIVE/DELETED, crn, approval_number, transporter_category), while OperatorResponse/AddressRequest and the generated docs/openapi/operators.yml emit camelCase addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode/phone/traceId/pageSize and a derived 'deleted' boolean, with no typed operator fields (OperatorComplianceIT explicitly asserts operatorType/transporterCategory/status are absent).
items.fix: Regenerate this file from the implemented model — camelCase properties, townOrCity/countryCode/phone, deleted boolean, no operator_type/status/crn/approval_number/transporter_category — and delete the PUT operator_type-immutability rule and TypeChangeProblemExample that reference a field the service does not have.

items.issue: The documented identity/scoping contract is wrong in a security-relevant way: CrnHeader (Trade-Imports-Crn, 'required on every request') is $ref'd into all five operations and the 400 examples say 'Missing required header Trade-Imports-Crn', but no CRN header exists anywhere in the service — IdentityHeaderFilter enforces Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id on every /organisation/** request and OperatorController.authoriseOrg compares it to the path orgId. The contract also states organisation-id is 'Required on POST only' and 'NOT used for read filtering today', the exact opposite of the implemented org-scoped reads.
items.fix: Replace CrnHeader with the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header as required on every operation, document the path-orgId vs session-org authorisation guard and its 404-on-mismatch behaviour, and update the BadRequestProblemExample detail to 'Missing required header Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id'.

items.issue: Both path items use the template variable {orgId} but neither declares an orgId path parameter (only operator-id is declared, at line 234), so the document is an invalid OpenAPI 3.0 file — swagger-parser/spectral/openapi-generator all fail it with 'Declared path parameter orgId needs to be defined as a path parameter at either the path or operation level'. The generated operators.yml does declare it, so the two disagree.
items.fix: Add an orgId path parameter (in: path, required: true, type: string) to the path-level parameters of both /organisation/{orgId}/addresses and /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{operator-id}.

items.issue: The preamble claims 'OperatorComplianceIT plus a CI diff check keep it honest' and that the generated operators.yml 'must stay equivalent to' this file, but OperatorComplianceIT.apiDocsMatchTheCommittedArtifactAndTheLockedContract only compares the path key set, the HTTP-method set, operationIds and the 400 anyOf — no schemas, parameters, headers or status codes. That is exactly why every divergence in this file is invisible to a green CI run.
items.fix: Either widen the divergence gate to compare parameters, response status codes and the referenced schema names, or downgrade the preamble claim to state precisely what is enforced (paths, methods, operationIds, anyOf 400).

items.issue: Deviation D1 states 'country is an MDM display-name string, NOT ISO 3166-1 alpha-2' and instructs reviewers not to 'fix' it, but the shipped AddressRequest/OperatorResponse field is countryCode carrying ISO alpha-2 ('GB' in OperatorComplianceIT and the list filter is ?countryCode=). The directive actively tells the next developer to revert the implemented behaviour. D2's page_size query parameter is likewise contradicted — page size is a server-side config, not a request parameter.
items.fix: Rewrite D1 to describe countryCode/ISO alpha-2 as implemented (or delete it), and drop page_size from D2 and from the list-operators parameter list.

items.issue: The list-operators parameter set does not match the implementation: the contract declares operator_type (enum filter) and page_size (min 1, max 100, default 25), while OperatorController.list accepts page, q and countryCode only; the contract also declares a 500 InternalError response on all five operations that no handler produces. A client generated from this file sends ?operator_type=&page_size= and silently gets unfiltered, server-sized pages.
items.fix: Replace operator_type with countryCode, drop page_size, and either remove the 500 responses or document them as the framework default.

items.issue: Stale pre-rename narrative survives the move to /organisation/{orgId}/addresses: line 13 says 'This file lives under workareas/, which is gitignored and absent from a clean CI checkout' while the file is committed at docs/openapi/; line 181 documents the 201 Location header as '/operators/{operator-id}' when the controller returns '/organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}'; the tag is 'operators' where the controller declares 'addresses'; and operationIds mix list-operators/create-operator with get-address/update-address/delete-address.
items.fix: Rewrite the preamble for the in-repo location, correct the Location header example and its schema example, rename the tag to 'addresses', and settle on one operationId noun.

items.issue: The POST/PUT 400 schema emits 'type: string' alongside the anyOf (lines 83 and 210), so the published contract says a problem+json 400 body is a JSON string; no object body validates and generated clients type the 400 as String, defeating the anyOf pin the design leans on.
items.fix: Give the @Content in OperatorController an explicit object type - @Schema(anyOf = {ValidationProblem.class, Problem.class}, type = "object") - or register a named composed schema, then regenerate with -Dopenapi.generate=true.

items.issue: This generated contract contradicts the in-repo docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml it is documented to be surface-equivalent to: camelCase vs snake_case properties, no Trade-Imports-Crn header, 'deleted' boolean vs 'status' enum, countryCode/phone/townOrCity vs country/telephone/town, no operator_type, no page_size param, no 500 responses, no Location header - OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares path set, HTTP methods and operationIds, so it cannot catch any of it
items.fix: Decide which document is the contract: either regenerate/rewrite api-contract.locked.yaml to the ruled camelCase model (and record the ruling that superseded it) or delete it, and widen OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate to compare parameters, request/response schemas and status-code sets - not just operationIds

items.issue: Every 2xx response is published under the wildcard media type '*/*' (lines 35, 75, 167, 202) instead of application/json, because each @ApiResponse in OperatorController overrides the 200/201 without a content block
items.fix: Give each 2xx @ApiResponse an explicit content = @Content(mediaType = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE, schema = @Schema(implementation = OperatorResponse.class / OperatorPageResponse.class)) and regenerate with -Dopenapi.generate=true

items.issue: AddressRequest publishes 'type' and 'role' as ordinary optional untyped ('type: object') request properties, but AddressRequest.java annotates both @Null so any supplied value is rejected with a 400 - a consumer following the contract will send them and fail
items.fix: Annotate both fields @Schema(hidden = true), or keep them visible with @Schema(description = "Not supported - omit; any value is rejected with a 400") plus an explicit constraint, then regenerate the artifact

items.issue: No response schema declares 'required': OperatorResponse (lines 297-330) marks all 14 fields optional despite OperatorResponse.java null-guarding 11 of them, and neither Problem (284) nor ValidationProblem (265) mandates anything - so ValidationProblem does not require 'errors', making the two 400 anyOf branches structurally identical open objects and defeating the anyOf-not-oneOf rationale the design leans on
items.fix: Add @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) to the non-nullable components of OperatorResponse, OperatorPageResponse, Problem (type/title/status) and ValidationProblem (plus errors), regenerate, and assert the ValidationProblem 'required: [errors]' in OperatorComplianceIT

items.issue: The published contract carries no descriptions at all - not one schema or property in components has a description, and the info block is springdoc's untouched default (title 'OpenAPI definition', version 'v0'), so consumers and generated SDKs get an unnamed, unversioned, undocumented API
items.fix: Add @Schema(description = ...) to AddressRequest, OperatorResponse, OperatorPageResponse, Problem and ValidationProblem and their fields, and add an @OpenAPIDefinition(info = @Info(title = "trade-imports-address-book", version = ...)) to OpenApiConfig, then regenerate

items.issue: Published constraints disagree with server validation: name, addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, phone and email carry minLength 0 (lines 221-252) although @NotBlank rejects an empty string with a 400, and the 'page' query param (line 148) has no minimum although an out-of-range page is a 400
items.fix: Use @Size(min = 1, max = ...) on the @NotBlank string components of AddressRequest and add @Min(1) (or @Schema(minimum = "1")) to the page parameter, then regenerate

items.issue: The 201 (line 199) does not document the Location header OperatorController.create actually returns, and no operation documents a 500 problem+json response even though GlobalExceptionHandler produces one - the locked contract declares both
items.fix: Add headers = @Header(name = "Location", ...) to the 201 @ApiResponse and a shared 500 @ApiResponse (mediaType application/problem+json, schema Problem) - via an OperationCustomizer if you do not want it repeated on all five operations - then regenerate

items.issue: Deleting RestClientConfig removes the only wiring of TraceIdPropagationInterceptor, which survives as an orphaned @Component (plus its test and the cdp.tracing.header-name property) whose Javadoc still claims it adds x-cdp-request-id to every outbound RestClient/RestTemplate call - it now adds it to none, so the stated CDP tracing requirement is silently unenforced for any future outbound client (the 10s connect / 30s read timeouts went with it too).

items.notes: Orphan interceptor cleanup completed: TraceIdPropagationInterceptor (+ test) deleted alongside RestClientConfig.

items.issue: Address has no @Version field, so the read-modify-write in OperatorService.update()/delete() is last-write-wins: repository.save() replaces the whole document, so a PUT that loaded an ACTIVE address and saves after a concurrent DELETE writes status=ACTIVE back and resurrects the tombstone (and two concurrent PUTs silently lose one edit).
items.fix: Add '@Version private Long version;' alongside the audit fields, add matching @Mapping(target="version", ignore=true) / ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties entries in OperatorMapper (unmappedTargetPolicy and unmappedSourcePolicy are both ERROR), and map OptimisticLockingFailureException to a 409 problem in GlobalExceptionHandler.

items.issue: The record's 11 components are the source of truth for the PUT full-replace body, but OperatorService.update hand-copies the 9 mappable ones with no compile-time link; OperatorMapper's unmappedSourcePolicy=ERROR forces a new component to be wired into toEntity (so POST keeps working) while update silently keeps ignoring it, so PUT quietly stops being a full replace
items.fix: Add a MapStruct in-place method to OperatorMapper - void updateEntity(AddressRequest request, @MappingTarget Address address) with the same id/organisationId/status/createdAt/modifiedAt ignores and type/role ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties - and call it from OperatorService.update instead of the nine setters, so an unmapped new field is a compile error on both paths

items.issue: New public API request record carries no @Schema on the record or any of its 11 components, so the generated OpenAPI contract has no descriptions, no examples, no requiredMode on the @NotBlank fields, and advertises the unsupported type/role as ordinary free-form Object properties
items.fix: Add @Schema(description=...) to the record and each component, set requiredMode = REQUIRED on the @NotBlank ones to match Bean Validation, and mark type/role @Schema(hidden = true) so the contract does not advertise fields the service rejects

items.issue: phone is the only component copied by OperatorService.update that no update test asserts - OperatorServiceTest.updateAppliesTheNewFieldValues checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/postcode/email and AddressUpdateIT checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode plus the cleared optionals, so deleting existing.setPhone(request.phone()) leaves the whole suite green
items.fix: Assert the replaced phone (and email) in AddressUpdateIT.putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals so every one of the nine copied fields is pinned by at least one update test

items.issue: countryCode is the only client-supplied string with no upper bound - every other component is @Size-capped - and it is persisted verbatim, so a caller can store an arbitrarily long value (AddressRequestValidationTest pins a 300-char value as valid); it is also indexed-adjacent via searchByCountryCode
items.fix: Add a generous defensive @Size(max = ...) alongside the @NotBlank - it caps abuse without introducing the ISO list check or the value transformation cv-011 rules out - and update the presence-only test to assert the cap rather than unlimited length

items.issue: create() builds the Location header by raw string concatenation into URI.create(); an orgId containing a URI-illegal character (e.g. a space, legal in an HTTP header value and reachable via a %20-encoded path segment that authoriseOrg accepts) throws IllegalArgumentException AFTER operatorService.create has persisted the address, so the caller gets a 500 and a retry creates a duplicate
items.fix: Build the URI with ServletUriComponentsBuilder.fromCurrentRequest().path("/{id}").buildAndExpand(created.getId()).toUri() (or UriComponentsBuilder with buildAndExpand) so the segments are encoded rather than concatenated; note OperatorCrudIT asserts Location startsWith a relative path, so keep the relative form or update that assertion

items.issue: list() and create() can return 404 (authoriseOrg on an org mismatch, proven by AddressScopingIT.forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404) but their @ApiResponses declare only 200/201 and 400, so the generated docs/openapi/operators.yml omits 404 for both operations and the published contract does not describe the actual behaviour
items.fix: Add @ApiResponse(responseCode = "404", content = @Content(mediaType = "application/problem+json", schema = @Schema(implementation = Problem.class))) to the list and create operations and regenerate docs/openapi/operators.yml with -Dopenapi.generate=true

items.issue: The 201 @ApiResponse on create() declares no Location header, so the generated spec documents no Location on POST even though the response sets one and consumers (AddressScopingIT, the frontend) parse it to obtain the new address id; the committed api-contract.locked.yaml does declare it, so the generated doc under-describes the agreed contract
items.fix: Add headers = @Header(name = "Location", description = "/organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{operator-id} of the created address", schema = @Schema(type = "string")) to the 201 @ApiResponse and regenerate the OpenAPI artifact

items.issue: Tenant scoping is correct today but structurally fragile: every handler passes the client-controlled path variable orgId (not the trusted sessionOrg header) to the service, and the authoriseOrg guard is hand-repeated in all five handlers, so a future handler that omits the one-line call would scope reads and writes to a value the caller controls with no compile-time or test-time signal
items.fix: Pass sessionOrg (the trusted forwarded header) to operatorService instead of orgId so the tenant id downstream is never client-controlled even if the guard is missed, and/or hoist the path-vs-header equality check into IdentityHeaderFilter or a HandlerInterceptor mapped to /organisation/{orgId}/** so it cannot be forgotten

items.issue: The published contract surface is internally inconsistent: the path template mixes camelCase {orgId} with kebab-case {operator-id} in the same mapping (Zalando requires kebab-case path segments), and the operationIds mix resource names for one resource - list-operators/create-operator versus get-address/update-address/delete-address - which generates clients with mismatched method names; OperatorComplianceIT locks these ids so the inconsistency becomes permanent once shipped
items.fix: Rename the path variable to {org-id} and settle on one noun for the operationIds (e.g. list-addresses/create-address/get-address/update-address/delete-address), then regenerate docs/openapi/operators.yml and update api-contract.locked.yaml

items.issue: The mapper covers create (toEntity) and read (toResponse) but has no @MappingTarget update method, so OperatorService.update copies the 9 mutable fields by hand; the compile-time guard this mapper advertises (unmappedTarget/SourcePolicy = ERROR) does not reach the PUT path, and a future field added to AddressRequest+Address will compile clean while PUT silently fails to replace it (stale value persists on a full-replace endpoint).
items.fix: Add 'void updateEntity(@MappingTarget Address entity, AddressRequest request)' with the same ignores as toEntity (id, organisationId, status, createdAt, modifiedAt; ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties type/role) and have OperatorService.update call it instead of the nine manual setters.

items.issue: No @Schema on the record or any component, so springdoc emits OperatorPageResponse with no 'required' array, no descriptions and no minimum bounds (docs/openapi/operators.yml lines 329-346) while the locked contract's OperatorPage declares items/page/page_size/total_items/total_pages all required with minimums (api-contract.locked.yaml lines 589-614); the compliance IT's divergence gate only compares path set + operationIds so the drift is unenforced.
items.fix: Add @Schema(description=...) on the record and @Schema(description=..., requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED, minimum=...) on each of items/page/pageSize/totalItems/totalPages, matching the locked contract's minimums (page>=1, pageSize>=1, totalItems>=0, totalPages>=0).

items.issue: The compact constructor null-guards items with Objects.requireNonNull but does not defensively copy it, so the record advertised as immutable keeps a live reference to whatever List the caller passed (OperatorService today passes an immutable Stream.toList(), but nothing enforces that on future callers or tests).
items.fix: Replace Objects.requireNonNull(items, "items") with items = List.copyOf(items); it both null-guards (List.copyOf throws NPE on null) and makes the component genuinely unmodifiable.

items.issue: Extending MongoRepository<Address, String> publishes unscoped id-only CRUD (findById, deleteById, delete, existsById, findAll, deleteAll) alongside the org-scoped finders, so the tenant guard the class javadoc claims (cv-010) is a convention, not a constraint
items.fix: Extend Repository<Address, String> and declare only what is used - save, the three org-scoped @Query searches, findByIdAndOrganisationId, findByOrganisationIdAndStatus (plus deleteAll for test cleanup) - so findById/deleteById are not on the interface at all

items.issue: The 'organisationId': ?0 term is the only tenant guard in the hand-written searchByCountryCode and searchByQueryAndCountryCode queries, and neither has a cross-org test - AddressSearchIT seeds OTHER_ORG only in searchIsOrgScopedAndExcludesSoftDeleted, which exercises the q-only searchByQuery path
items.fix: In AddressSearchIT, add an OTHER_ORG (and a DELETED) row to countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code and combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode, asserting totalItems excludes them

items.issue: The three @Query methods hard-code the string literal 'ACTIVE' for status while findByOrganisationIdAndStatus binds the AddressStatus enum, so the persisted status representation now has two sources of truth
items.fix: Bind status as a parameter in the raw queries ('status': ?N) and pass AddressStatus.ACTIVE from OperatorService.queryPage, matching the derived method

items.issue: Response shape contradicts docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (committed in this same PR) on every property: locked Operator is snake_case with required crn, status enum and operator_type plus address_line_1/town/country/telephone; OperatorResponse emits camelCase addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode/phone, a derived deleted boolean, and drops crn and operator_type entirely - so the PR ships two committed contract documents that disagree field-for-field
items.fix: Re-issue api-contract.locked.yaml to the ruled untyped camelCase model (or revert the record to the locked shape), and extend OperatorComplianceIT.apiDocsMatchTheCommittedArtifactAndTheLockedContract to diff components.schemas property names - today it only compares path set, HTTP methods and operationIds, so the schema divergence passes the gate the Javadoc claims it enforces
items.notes: Locked contract regenerated to camelCase OperatorResponse matching the Java record; original snake_case contradiction is gone.

items.issue: countryCode reverses declared deviation D1 of the locked contract, which rules country is an MDM display-name string (e.g. 'United Kingdom'), NOT ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, and states reviewers must not silently 'fix' it; Address.java documents countryCode as ISO alpha-2 (cv-011), so this is a value-semantics change not just a rename - a consumer rendering the address gets 'GB' where the contract promises 'United Kingdom' and D1 records that no code-to-name conversion exists anywhere in the epic
items.fix: Either emit the MDM display name as country, or record the superseding ruling in api-contract.locked.yaml (replacing D1) and confirm the frontend/animals-backend consumers resolve alpha-2 to a display name before render

items.issue: No @Schema on the record or any component, so the committed docs/openapi/operators.yml renders OperatorResponse with zero field descriptions and no required list - all 14 fields generate as optional in consumer client SDKs even though 11 are guaranteed non-null by the compact constructor
items.fix: Add a class-level @Schema(description=...) and per-component @Schema(description=..., example=..., requiredMode=Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) for the 11 guarded fields (leave addressLine2/county default), then regenerate the artifact with mvn verify -Dopenapi.generate=true

items.issue: The 11 compact-constructor null guards are new behaviour with no test: OperatorMapperTest covers field-by-field mapping, the derived deleted boolean and camelCase serialisation, but nothing asserts a null id/name/countryCode/organisationId/createdAt throws, so the documented 'fails loud' contract is unverified and a guard could be dropped silently
items.fix: Add a parameterised OperatorResponseTest asserting NullPointerException with the field name as message for each guarded component, and that addressLine2/county accept null

items.issue: update() hand-copies the nine client fields with setters instead of a MapStruct @MappingTarget method, so the mapper's unmappedTargetPolicy=ERROR guard (which protects toEntity/toResponse) does not cover the PUT path: add a field to AddressRequest+Address and toEntity fails the build while update() silently keeps compiling and PUT retains stale data for the new field.
items.fix: Add 'void updateEntity(AddressRequest request, @MappingTarget Address address)' to OperatorMapper with the same @Mapping(ignore) set for id/organisationId/status/createdAt/modifiedAt and ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties {type, role}, and call it from update() in place of the nine setters, so a future field addition is a compile-time failure rather than a silent stale-data bug.

items.issue: The PUT full-replace of 'phone' is asserted nowhere: OperatorServiceTest.updateAppliesTheNewFieldValues... checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/postcode/email only, AddressUpdateIT.putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals checks name plus the cleared addressLine2/county, and OperatorCrudIT checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode - so deleting 'existing.setPhone(request.phone())' leaves the stale telephone number on the document and the whole suite still passes.
items.fix: Assert the replaced phone value in OperatorServiceTest.updateAppliesTheNewFieldValuesBumpsModifiedAtAndPreservesTheServerOwnedFields (assertThat(updated.getPhone()).isEqualTo("+44 1738 111222")) and in AddressUpdateIT.putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals, and while there add the missing addressLine2 set-to-a-new-value case so every one of the nine replaced fields has at least one assertion.

items.issue: The list timer is registered as 'OperatorListQuery' - PascalCase, breaking the dot-delimited Micrometer convention used everywhere else in the service ('controller.listOperators.time', best-practice 'notification.save'), and more importantly EmfMetricsPublisher.publishMetrics() only removes meters whose name startsWith("controller"), so this meter is never reset and its cumulative COUNT and TOTAL_TIME are re-emitted to CloudWatch on every 60s publish cycle - the metric grows monotonically instead of reporting the interval's activity.
items.fix: Rename the timer to a dot-delimited, controller-prefix-consistent name that EmfMetricsPublisher's reset filter picks up (e.g. meterRegistry.timer("controller.listOperators.query.time")), or widen the reset filter in EmfMetricsPublisher to cover service meters; also wrap the query in try/finally so the sample is stopped when queryPage throws.

items.issue: propertyNamingStrategy(LOWER_CAMEL_CASE) makes the whole HTTP boundary camelCase (addressLine1, townOrCity, traceId), directly contradicting the committed docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml, which mandates snake_case JSON properties throughout (address_line_1, created_at, organisation_id, and trace_id described there as 'a deliberate divergence from the animals-backend camelCase'), and the rest-api best practice ('snake_case for properties', 'Don't: camelCase in JSON'); OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares paths/HTTP methods/operationIds, so the property-name reversal passes CI unnoticed
items.fix: Pick one and make it explicit: either drop this customizer (or switch to PropertyNamingStrategies.SNAKE_CASE plus @JsonProperty for the address_line_1 style names SNAKE_CASE cannot derive) to honour the locked contract, or reissue/retire api-contract.locked.yaml as camelCase with the decision recorded, and extend the compliance IT's divergence gate to compare component-schema property names so the two can never silently disagree again

items.issue: The customizer pins two contract-visible Jackson knobs (naming, unknown properties) but leaves date/time serialisation to the Spring Boot default, and no test asserts it: OperatorResponse exposes Instant createdAt/modifiedAt which the contract declares as RFC 3339 date-time strings, yet OperatorComplianceIT only asserts jsonPath('$.createdAt').exists() — a later spring.jackson.serialization.write-dates-as-timestamps=true would silently turn them into epoch numbers with a green build
items.fix: Either add .featuresToDisable(SerializationFeature.WRITE_DATES_AS_TIMESTAMPS) here to pin the behaviour explicitly alongside the other two knobs, or tighten OperatorComplianceIT to assert createdAt/modifiedAt match an ISO-8601 instant pattern rather than merely existing

items.issue: The whole class is a no-op: setupServiceVersion() writes a JVM system property 'service.version' that nothing ever reads — logback-spring.xml resolves service.version via <springProperty name="service.version" source="cdp.service-version"/>, and a springProperty always shadows a same-named system property; worse, @PostConstruct fires long after Logback has initialised, so a system property set here could never influence the encoder even if the XML did read it.
items.fix: Delete LoggingConfig (EcsLoggingIT's service.version assertion is satisfied by the springProperty/<serviceVersion> wiring alone); if a real system property is ever needed for logging, set it from an EnvironmentPostProcessor that runs before LoggingApplicationListener.

items.issue: MDC key naming is inconsistent with RequestTracingFilter: there the MDC_* constants (MDC_TRACE_ID, MDC_HTTP_METHOD, MDC_URL_FULL) really are MDC.put keys, whereas MDC_SERVICE_VERSION here is used as a System.setProperty key and the class Javadoc claims it 'Sets up service version in MDC' — nothing in this class touches MDC.
items.fix: If the class survives, rename the constant to SERVICE_VERSION_PROPERTY and correct the Javadoc; otherwise remove it with the class.

items.issue: org.springframework.boot.info.BuildProperties and java.util.Optional are imported but never used; the pom has no spotless/checkstyle/PMD plugin, so nothing in the build will catch them.

items.issue: No @EnableScheduling anywhere in the app (grep of src finds none, Application.java has only @SpringBootApplication + @EnableConfigurationProperties), so EmfMetricsPublisher's @Scheduled(fixedRate = 60000) publishMetrics() never fires and no EMF metric is ever flushed to CloudWatch — MetricsConfigurationPropertiesTest asserts the annotation exists but nothing proves it runs

items.issue: The PR adds @EnableMongoAuditing here, which turns on @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate but NOT optimistic locking — Address has no @Version field, so OperatorService.update() and delete() are unguarded read-modify-write full-document save() calls (last-write-wins; a concurrent delete can be resurrected by an in-flight PUT). Corroborates the open cross-file finding on Address.java.
items.fix: Add a @Version Long field to Address so Spring Data emits a version-predicated update, and map the resulting OptimisticLockingFailureException to 409 in GlobalExceptionHandler (or switch update/delete to a targeted findAndModify with a status/version predicate instead of save()).

items.issue: Javadoc claims the ModelResolver stops /v3/api-docs diverging from 'the locked contract - the exact divergence OperatorComplianceIT fails the build on', but that gate (OperatorComplianceIT lines 231-251) compares only path keys, HTTP-method keys and operationIds against docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml; components.schemas, parameters, securitySchemes and info are never compared, so the locked contract's snake_case operator_type/crn/approval_number/transporter_category fields and its Trade-Imports-Crn header pass green despite existing nowhere in the code
items.fix: Withdraw the overclaim (the resolver only binds swagger-core to the app ObjectMapper) and extend OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate to also compare components.schemas property-name sets and operation parameter names, so a locked contract documenting fields the service does not implement fails the build

items.issue: OpenApiConfig declares no @OpenAPIDefinition and no OpenAPI bean, so the spec published at /v3/api-docs and committed as docs/openapi/operators.yml carries springdoc placeholders 'title: OpenAPI definition' and 'version: v0' (operators.yml lines 3-4) with no servers block (OperatorComplianceIT line 210 strips servers before writing) - an untitled, unversioned, base-URL-less artifact that README line 185 advertises as committed 'for downstream consumers', and that contradicts the locked contract's title trade-imports-address-book / version 1.0.0 / servers block
items.fix: Add @OpenAPIDefinition(info = @Info(title = "trade-imports-address-book", version = "1.0.0", description = ...)) to this class and an @Bean OpenAPI declaring the deployed servers, so the generated document carries real identity and matches api-contract.locked.yaml lines 2-4 and 76

items.issue: No SecurityScheme is declared here, so the identity contract is documented two incompatible ways and nothing reconciles them: the generated spec models Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id as a per-operation @RequestHeader parameter (operators.yml lines 21/55/104/141/187) while api-contract.locked.yaml lines 376-396 declares securitySchemes Trade-Imports-Crn AND Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id, with Trade-Imports-Crn described as the primary identity header - IdentityHeaderFilter lines 46/73 reads only Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id and 400s otherwise, so a consumer coding to the locked contract sends Trade-Imports-Crn and is rejected
items.fix: Declare a single apiKey-in-header SecurityScheme for Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id in an @Bean OpenAPI here plus a matching @SecurityRequirement, and delete the Trade-Imports-Crn scheme and its narrative from api-contract.locked.yaml since no code enforces it

items.issue: new ModelResolver(objectMapper) hands swagger-core the application's singleton ObjectMapper; swagger-core's AbstractModelConverter constructor calls mapper.registerModule(...) which inserts SwaggerAnnotationIntrospector into that mapper, so swagger annotations begin influencing real HTTP serialisation (hasRequiredMarker, findSubtypes, findTypeName) and not just the generated document
items.fix: Pass a copy - new ModelResolver(objectMapper.copy()) - which keeps the JacksonConfig LOWER_CAMEL_CASE strategy the Javadoc relies on while leaving the runtime mapper unmutated

items.issue: Both the invalid-format warn (line 59) and the parse-failure error (line 77) log the raw httpProxy value; CDP proxy URLs are of the form http://user:password@host:port, so a malformed value (e.g. missing scheme) leaks proxy credentials into CloudWatch logs
items.fix: Log a redacted form only - strip userinfo before logging (e.g. httpProxy.replaceAll("//[^@/]+@", "//***@")), or log just the fact that parsing failed plus proxyUri.getHost()

items.issue: ProxySelector.of() builds a selector with no bypass list and http.nonProxyHosts/https.nonProxyHosts are never set, so once HTTP_PROXY is present every outbound HTTP call - including localhost targets such as the cdp.cloudwatch.endpoint default http://localhost:4566, actuator self-calls and any in-test WireMock stub - is forced through the proxy and will fail; the class Javadoc's claim that no bypass is needed only covers *.cdp-int.defra.cloud routing by the squid proxy, not loopback
items.fix: Set System.setProperty("http.nonProxyHosts", "localhost|127.*|[::1]|*.cdp-int.defra.cloud") (and the https equivalent) and use a ProxySelector implementation that honours it rather than the unconditional ProxySelector.of(...)

items.issue: configureProxy() has no effective test coverage: ProxyConfigIT gates every meaningful assertion on System.getenv("HTTP_PROXY") being set, which it never is in CI, so the tests degrade to assertThat(proxyConfig).isNotNull() and a literal assertThat(true).isTrue() - none of the four branches (blank, invalid host/port, parse failure, happy path) is exercised
items.fix: Extract the parsing into a package-private method taking the proxy URL as an argument and unit-test it directly, or drive the Spring context with @TestPropertySource(properties = "cdp.proxyUrl=http://localhost:3128") plus negative cases, so the branches are asserted without depending on the OS environment

items.issue: configureProxy() mutates JVM-global state (four System properties plus ProxySelector.setDefault) from @PostConstruct and never restores it; ProxyConfigIT's @AfterAll clears the system properties but not the default ProxySelector, so once any test context sets a proxy it stays set for every later test class in the same Surefire/Failsafe JVM
items.fix: Prefer configuring a ProxyConfiguration on the specific RestClient/HttpClient builder the service uses; if the global approach is kept for CDP parity, capture and restore the previous ProxySelector in the test and document the global mutation as a deliberate CDP requirement

items.issue: Any userinfo in the proxy URL (http://user:pass@host:port) is silently discarded - only host and port are propagated and no java.net.Authenticator is installed - so against an authenticated proxy every request fails with 407 and the logs say the proxy was configured successfully
items.fix: Read proxyUri.getUserInfo(); if present, install an Authenticator (and set jdk.http.auth.tunneling.disabledSchemes="" for HTTPS CONNECT), or log a warn that credentials in HTTP_PROXY are not supported so the failure mode is visible

items.issue: The no-proxy guard uses isEmpty() rather than isBlank(), so a whitespace-only HTTP_PROXY (easy to produce from a CDP env-var template) falls through to URI.create(" "), throws IllegalArgumentException and is reported as an ERROR instead of taking the benign 'no proxy configured' path
items.fix: Use if (httpProxy == null || httpProxy.isBlank()) and strip() the value before URI.create - modern-java.md prefers isBlank()/strip() over isEmpty()/trim()

items.issue: cdp.proxyUrl is injected with @Value onto a private field, which is the field-injection anti-pattern the Spring Boot guide bans (section 7: always constructor injection, never field injection); it also makes the class untestable without a Spring context, which is why ProxyConfigIT is reduced to null checks
items.fix: Take the value as a constructor parameter - public ProxyConfig(@Value("${cdp.proxyUrl}") String httpProxy) - and assign to a final field

items.issue: cert == null conflates 'no CDP cert configured' with 'cert configured but unparseable' (CertificateLoader.loadCustomCertificate swallows CertificateException and returns null), so a corrupt TRUSTSTORE_CDP_ROOT_CA boots successfully with the default JVM trust store only and fails later at Mongo/CDP TLS connect time instead of at startup
items.fix: Make CertificateLoader rethrow (e.g. IllegalStateException) when the cdp.certificate property is non-empty but fails to parse, or have it return an Optional plus a 'configured' flag so customSslContext() can fail fast; keep the silent path only for the genuinely-unset case

items.issue: log.info hardcodes 'initialized successfully with 1 custom certificate' on every path, including when createCombinedTrustManager returned the default-only trust manager because cert was null - operations see '1 custom certificate' precisely when zero were loaded, masking the degradation above
items.fix: Log the real outcome, e.g. move the message inside the branches or log 'custom certificates loaded: {}' with (cert == null ? 0 : 1)

items.issue: @Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE) plus the class javadoc claim that it 'ensures the SSLContext is available before other beans (like MongoClient) are created' is untrue - @Order on a @Configuration class affects configuration-class ordering, not bean instantiation timing; ordering here is actually guaranteed by MongoConfig injecting TrustStoreConfiguration
items.fix: Drop the @Order annotation and the Ordered import, and correct the javadoc to say ordering comes from dependency injection

items.issue: CombinedTrustManager.checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted discard the default trust manager's CertificateException when falling through to the custom trust manager, so when both reject a chain only the custom CDP trust manager's (usually less informative) error surfaces and the real public-CA failure reason is lost
items.fix: Capture the first exception and attach it via addSuppressed on the exception thrown by the custom trust manager (or log it at debug) before rethrowing

items.issue: createCombinedTrustManager declares 'throws Exception' and customSslContext catches bare Exception, which trips Sonar java:S112 and also swallows unrelated runtime faults (NPE, bean-wiring errors) behind the misleading 'Cannot initialize SSL context' message
items.fix: Narrow to 'throws GeneralSecurityException, IOException' on the helper and catch the same specific types in customSslContext

items.issue: Class Javadoc names two triggers that never throw this exception: a missing identity header is rejected inside IdentityHeaderFilter (which writes problem+json itself because @RestControllerAdvice cannot see filter exceptions) and a malformed query parameter surfaces as MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException with its own handler; the sole production throw site is OperatorService.list for an out-of-range page (< 1).
items.fix: Reword the Javadoc to describe the real trigger (a request parameter that is syntactically valid but out of range, e.g. page < 1) and drop the missing-identity-header and malformed-query-param examples, so nobody throws this from a servlet filter expecting the advice to map it.

items.issue: The RuntimeException catch-all swallows Spring's own runtime client-error exceptions: HttpMessageNotReadableException extends NestedRuntimeException, and spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled is not set anywhere in src/main/resources, so Spring's ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler is not registered — a POST/PUT with a truncated or absent JSON body returns 500 internal-error (logged at ERROR with a full stack trace) instead of the contract's 400 bad-request, exactly the fall-through the new handleTypeMismatch handler was added to close.
items.fix: Add an @ExceptionHandler(HttpMessageNotReadableException.class) returning the bad-request problem (same shape as handleTypeMismatch), plus an IT posting a malformed body; consider narrowing the catch-all or setting spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled.

items.issue: The handler emits camelCase problem fields (traceId property, errors keyed by the Java field name e.g. addressLine1) but the in-repo docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml at this commit still declares trace_id and 'Map of snake_case wire field name -> list of messages' (keys 'address_line_1, never addressLine1'), so the declared source of truth contradicts the shipped wire; OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares path sets, HTTP methods and operationIds, so the drift passes CI unnoticed.
items.fix: Update the Problem/ValidationProblem schemas, the info description and the ValidationProblemExample/TypeChangeProblemExample in docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml to camelCase (cv-001), and extend the divergence gate to compare component-schema property names, not just operationIds.

items.issue: The record's traceId member contradicts docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml, which declares Problem.trace_id in snake_case and documents it as 'a deliberate divergence from the animals-backend's camelCase traceId' — the exact opposite of this Javadoc's cv-001 rationale; OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares path sets and operationIds, so the drift passes CI unnoticed.
items.fix: Pick one source of truth and make the other follow: if cv-001 camelCase stands (as the IT and generated operators.yml assert), update the locked contract's Problem/ValidationProblem schemas to traceId and drop the snake_case rationale text; otherwise rename the record member. Consider extending the IT's divergence gate to compare component schema property names, not just paths and operationIds.

items.issue: The record carries no @Schema annotations, so the generated docs/openapi/operators.yml Problem schema has no description, no examples and — critically — no required list, while the locked contract declares required: [type, title, status]; every 400/404/500 response in the published contract therefore advertises all five members as optional to generated clients.
items.fix: Annotate the record type with @Schema(description = "RFC 9457 problem details") and each component with @Schema(description = ..., example = ...), adding requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED on type, title and status (leave detail and traceId optional). Apply the same to ValidationProblem so its errors member is marked required as the contract's allOf branch requires.

items.issue: errors map SHAPE (Map<field,List<message>>) matches the handler and the contract, but the CASING contradicts the in-repo docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml added by this same PR: the locked ValidationProblem says keys are 'ALWAYS the wire names (address_line_1, never addressLine1)' and Problem declares trace_id, while this record declares traceId and its Javadoc mandates camelCase keys; camelCase is not in the contract's 'Declared deviations' list and OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate compares only path sets, HTTP methods, operationIds and the 400 anyOf, so the schema-level drift ships silently
items.fix: Re-copy the locked contract with camelCase Problem/ValidationProblem schemas, examples and prose (traceId, errors keyed addressLine1) recorded as a cv-001 deviation — the code, ITs and ins-frontend (errors.addressLine1) are all camelCase — and extend the divergence gate to compare schema property names so this cannot drift again

items.issue: No @Schema(requiredMode = REQUIRED) on any component, so springdoc emits ValidationProblem (and Problem) with no required list at all — see the committed docs/openapi/operators.yml ValidationProblem schema, which has properties but no 'required'. The locked contract declares ValidationProblem as allOf [Problem, {required: [errors]}] with Problem requiring type/title/status; the published spec therefore makes 'errors' — the one field that distinguishes the validation-error branch from the bad-request branch — optional, and generated clients get a nullable map on the commonest 400
items.fix: Annotate the record components with @Schema(requiredMode = Schema.RequiredMode.REQUIRED) on type, title, status and errors (leave detail/traceId optional) and regenerate docs/openapi/operators.yml with -Dopenapi.generate=true

items.issue: The 'trusted forwarded header' Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id is read straight off the client request with nothing establishing the trust: the repo has no Spring Security (no starter in pom.xml, no SecurityFilterChain), no gateway/ingress config and no documented requirement that an upstream strips inbound copies of the header, so any caller able to reach the service can read, create, amend or delete any organisation's address PII by setting one header
items.fix: Establish and document the trust boundary before this ships: strip/overwrite Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id at the CDP ingress or the calling BFF, and add either an authenticated principal check (JWT resource server) or an explicit allowlist of the forwarding hop in this filter; at minimum record the boundary and its owner in README plus an IT that proves a direct caller cannot self-assert an org id

items.issue: The whole tenant guard hangs on a raw string test, httpRequest.getRequestURI().startsWith("/organisation"), so it silently fails OPEN the moment the request URI stops starting with that literal - setting server.servlet.context-path, mounting the app under a path prefix, or any ingress that forwards a rewritten path disables enforcement on every endpoint with no test failing; it also over-matches unrelated paths such as /organisation-summary
items.fix: Let the container do the matching: register the filter with a FilterRegistrationBean using addUrlPatterns("/organisation/*"), or extend OncePerRequestFilter and implement shouldNotFilter with a PathPatternParser/AntPathMatcher over getServletPath() so the context path is excluded by construction; add an IT asserting a request under a configured context path is still rejected without the header
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: The filter only proves the header is PRESENT; the actual cross-tenant check (header value equals path orgId) is hand-repeated as the first line of all five OperatorController handlers via authoriseOrg, so the guard is opt-in per method - a future handler under /organisation/** that omits @RequestHeader + authoriseOrg gets zero cross-org protection and nothing in the build fails, even though the filter already holds both the path and the header value
items.fix: Move the match into the filter: parse the {orgId} segment from the gated path and reject a mismatch centrally (keeping the 404 no-existence-disclosure shape), leaving authoriseOrg in the controller only as a redundant assertion; alternatively add an architecture test asserting every handler method mapped under /organisation/{orgId} calls authoriseOrg
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: The finally MDC.remove(organisationId) is the only thing stopping one tenant's id bleeding onto the next request on a pooled Tomcat thread, yet IdentityHeaderFilterTest only asserts the value is PRESENT during the chain (validHeader_proceedsAndOrganisationIdLandsInMdcDuringTheChain) - there is no assertion that it is gone after doFilter returns, and none that it is still removed when the chain throws, so deleting the finally would leave the suite green
items.fix: Add two cases to IdentityHeaderFilterTest: after a successful doFilter assert MDC.get("organisationId") is null, and with a chain that throws a RuntimeException assert the exception propagates AND MDC.get("organisationId") is null afterwards
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: Implements the raw jakarta.servlet.Filter rather than extending OncePerRequestFilter, so it hand-rolls the HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse instanceof narrowing and the path check that shouldNotFilter exists for, and gains no protection against re-running on a FORWARD/ASYNC dispatch if the registration's dispatcher types are ever widened - the sibling RequestTracingFilter has the same shape, and the workspace Spring Boot guide models filters on OncePerRequestFilter
items.fix: Extend OncePerRequestFilter, move the path test into shouldNotFilter and drop the instanceof narrowing from doFilterInternal
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: The security-critical header name is declared twice as independent literals - IdentityHeaderFilter.ORGANISATION_ID_HEADER here and a private copy in OperatorController line 44 (plus a third in each IT) - so renaming one leaves the filter gating on a header the controller no longer binds, or vice versa, with no compile error
items.fix: Promote one public constant (e.g. an IdentityHeaders holder in the filter package) and have OperatorController and the ITs import it rather than restating the literal
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: isBlank is the only validation applied to the value that becomes the tenant key: an arbitrary-length, arbitrary-charset client string is pushed into the MDC (so it lands in every ECS log line for the request) and, on POST, is persisted verbatim as Address.organisationId, giving an unbounded attacker-controlled field in both the log store and Mongo
items.fix: Reject a value that does not match a bounded pattern (for example ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$) with the same 400 bad-request problem, so the tenant key is a known shape before it reaches MDC or the repository
items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest

items.issue: http.response.status_code is put into MDC after chain.doFilter returns and is wiped by MDC.clear() in the finally block, so no log line ever carries it (and it is skipped entirely when the chain throws) - the ECS field the class javadoc promises is never emitted; carried through unchanged by this PR's package rename
items.fix: Either drop the MDC_HTTP_STATUS put, or emit a single request-completion log line (log.info) immediately after setting it, before the finally clears MDC; add an EcsLoggingIT assertion for http.response.status_code
items.notes: Verified gone in RequestTracingFilter refresh: dead http.response.status_code MDC put removed.

items.issue: Interceptor is never registered: this PR deletes RestClientConfig (the only place that wired it via RestClient.Builder.requestInterceptor / RestTemplateBuilder.interceptors), and Spring Boot does not auto-apply ClientHttpRequestInterceptor beans to the auto-configured builders, so the @Component is instantiated but never runs and the Javadoc claim that it adds the header to 'every outbound HTTP call made via RestClient or RestTemplate' is now false
items.fix: Either delete the interceptor and its test until an outbound HTTP client exists, or add a RestClientCustomizer/RestTemplateCustomizer @Bean that registers it (and correct the Javadoc to say the header name is configurable via cdp.tracing.header-name)

items.issue: publishMetrics() never runs: '@EnableScheduling' appears nowhere in the repo (grep across all of src returns nothing) and no production code calls publishMetrics() - only tests do - so Spring never registers a ScheduledAnnotationBeanPostProcessor and the whole EMF publication path is dead code despite the aws.emf.* config and CDP CloudWatch endpoint being wired up
items.fix: Add '@EnableScheduling' to Application (or a SchedulingConfig '@Configuration' class as per spring-boot.md section 11) and back it with an integration test that asserts the scheduled task is actually registered, not just that the annotation is present

items.issue: Every measurement is published under the bare meter name - both Meter.Id tags and Measurement.getStatistic() are discarded - so a Timer's COUNT, TOTAL_TIME and MAX all collapse into one metric key, and the ~8 differently-tagged jvm.memory.used meters (area x pool) merge into a single unusable series; unit is also lost (defaults to Unit.NONE) even though timers are in nanoseconds
items.fix: Qualify the EMF key with the statistic (e.g. name + '.' + measurement.getStatistic().getTagValueRepresentation()), pass the correct Unit, and emit the meter's low-cardinality tags as EMF dimensions via putDimensions(DimensionSet) so series stay distinguishable

items.issue: putMetric() is called with no guard: aws-embedded-metrics 4.2.0 Validator.validateMetric throws the unchecked InvalidMetricException when !Double.isFinite(value), and Micrometer gauges legitimately report NaN (e.g. a gauge whose weak reference has been collected), so one NaN aborts the forEach before flush() at line 47 and silently drops every metric for that cycle - recurring every 60s while the bad meter exists
items.fix: Skip non-finite measurements (if (!Double.isFinite(value)) return;) and wrap the publish body in try/catch logging at WARN so metric publication is best-effort and flush() still runs; add a unit test covering a NaN gauge

items.issue: The publisher destructively mutates the shared application MeterRegistry every 60s, removing every meter whose name startsWith the undocumented magic string 'controller' - this wipes those series from the exposed actuator /metrics endpoint and leaves mixed semantics, since controller.* is published as a per-minute delta while all other meters (jvm.*, http.server.requests.active) are published as cumulative totals
items.fix: Drop the removal and let CloudWatch derive rates from cumulative counters, or publish into a dedicated per-window registry that is not the shared bean; if the reset must stay, extract the prefix to a named constant and document the delta-vs-cumulative split. Also reuse the single getMeters() result instead of calling it twice

items.issue: MetricsLogger is constructed inline inside publishMetrics(), so nothing published to EMF can be asserted - EmfMetricsPublisherTest can only verify(meterRegistry, times(2)).getMeters(), which asserts implementation detail rather than any published namespace, metric name or value
items.fix: Inject a Supplier<MetricsLogger> (or a thin MetricsLoggerFactory bean) so tests can capture the logger and assert the namespace, metric keys and values actually emitted

items.issue: The bean is gated on management.metrics.enabled, but application.yml defines a dedicated aws.emf.enabled flag (line 42) that no code reads - so EMF publication cannot be switched off independently of Micrometer, and the dedicated flag is dead configuration
items.fix: Gate on the purpose-built flag: '@ConditionalOnProperty(name = "aws.emf.enabled", havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = false)', and update MetricsConfigurationPropertiesTest accordingly - or delete aws.emf.enabled from application.yml if the coarser gate is intended

items.issue: Unused imports carried into the renamed package: io.micrometer.core.instrument.composite.CompositeMeterRegistry (line 4) and java.util.List (line 5) are never referenced (Sonar java:S1128)
items.fix: Delete both import statements

items.issue: Correcting the logger key from the non-existent package 'uk.gov.defra.trade.imports.address.book' to the real 'uk.gov.defra.trade.imports.addressbook' activates a previously-inert DEBUG default, so every deployed environment that does not set LOG_LEVEL now logs the whole application package at DEBUG (root is only ${LOG_LEVEL:info}, and application-integration-test.yml deliberately uses ${LOG_LEVEL:INFO}).
items.fix: Change the default to ${LOG_LEVEL:INFO} in application.yml; application-local.yml already sets this package to DEBUG for local work, so nothing is lost.

items.issue: swagger-ui is correctly disabled, but springdoc.api-docs is left at its default (enabled) in every deployed environment; the justifying comment cites the committed contract artifact and OperatorComplianceIT, both of which only read /v3/api-docs at build/test time (OperatorComplianceIT hits http://localhost:{port}/v3/api-docs on a locally booted context), and it cites a 'design §1.6' document that does not exist in the repo.

items.issue: The 'over-length email' case (repeat(243) + "@example.com") also violates @Email — Hibernate Validator 8 caps the local part at 64 chars — so with the assertion checking only the property path, @Size(max = 254) on email is never independently exercised and would survive deletion, contradicting the class Javadoc claim to pin 'every max-length'.
items.fix: Use a format-valid 255-character address (local part <= 64 chars plus a long multi-label domain) so only @Size can fire, or assert the violated constraint annotation rather than just the path.

items.issue: countryCodeIsPresenceOnlyAndAcceptsAnyNonBlankValueRegardlessOfLength pins a 300-character countryCode as VALID, turning an unvalidated field into an asserted contract: AddressRequest, Address and OperatorRepository all document countryCode as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, yet it carries @NotBlank only and is persisted verbatim and used in Mongo equality/regex queries, so arbitrary-length client text is accepted and stored.
items.fix: Add @Size(max = 2) (or @Pattern("^[A-Za-z]{2}$")) to AddressRequest.countryCode and rewrite this test as an over-length/malformed rejection case; if the gap is a deliberate deferral, drop the 300-char pin and record it as a known limitation instead of asserting it as intended behaviour.

items.issue: invalidFieldProducesAViolationOnThatField asserts only the violated property path, so none of the ten bespoke user-facing messages declared on AddressRequest ('Enter a name', 'Postcode must be 12 characters or less', ...) is asserted anywhere in the repo — the ITs assert only errors.<field> exists and GlobalExceptionHandlerTest hand-builds FieldError copies rather than reading the record's declared messages.
items.fix: Add the expected message as a fourth column of the invalidFields Arguments and assert that a violation exists with that property path AND that message (e.g. extracting propertyPath/message tuples), so the GDS error copy is pinned where the constraints are declared.

items.issue: The @Size matrix is one-sided: every sized field is probed at max+1 only, and the valid fixture values are short, so tightening any limit (e.g. name to @Size(max = 10)) leaves the whole suite green even though the field table and the error copy promise 255/100/12/20/254.
items.fix: Add a companion parameterized case per sized field at exactly the maximum (255/255/255/100/100/12/20/254) asserting no violations, so both edges of each declared max are pinned.

items.issue: The camelCase 'contract lock' test builds its own ObjectMapper and sets LOWER_CAMEL_CASE + failOnUnknownProperties(false) itself, so it asserts the strategy the test just configured, not the production JacksonConfig — deleting JacksonConfig entirely leaves this test green; the assertions are also presence-only (json.has) so a field serialising as null still passes
items.fix: Drop the hand-built mapper: either move this method into a @JsonTest/@SpringBootTest slice that injects the Spring-managed ObjectMapper (or applies JacksonConfig's Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer to a builder), and assert values not just key presence (json.get("addressLine1").asText() etc.); if the real-stack coverage in OperatorComplianceIT is deemed sufficient, delete this method rather than keep a tautology named as a contract lock

items.issue: request_deserialisesFromCamelCaseAndMapsOntoAnEntityIgnoringServerFields asserts entity.getOrganisationId() and entity.getStatus() are null under the comment 'Server-assigned fields in the body are ignored', but the JSON body carries neither an organisationId nor a status key — only id and deleted — so both assertions are unfalsifiable; no test in the repo posts an organisationId in a body, leaving the cv-010 tenant-smuggling guard entirely unexercised
items.fix: Add "organisationId": "OTHER-ORG", "status": "DELETED", "createdAt"/"modifiedAt" values to the body so the null assertions can actually fail, and add a matching AddressScopingIT case posting organisationId=ORG_B as ORG_A and asserting the persisted row is still ORG_A

items.issue: sampleEntity always populates all 14 fields, so no test ever maps an entity with the genuinely optional addressLine2/county absent, and none of OperatorResponse's 11 Objects.requireNonNull guards (id, name, addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, createdAt, modifiedAt) is exercised — a repo-wide grep for requireNonNull/NullPointerException/assertThatThrownBy/assertThrows in src/test returns nothing, so the deliberate fail-loud behaviour on a legacy or partially-written Mongo row is unpinned
items.fix: Add two cases: toResponse on an entity with null addressLine2 and null county maps cleanly (guards stay off the optional fields), and assertThatThrownBy(() -> operatorMapper.toResponse(entityWithNullPhone)).isInstanceOf(NullPointerException.class).hasMessage("phone") to pin at least one required-field guard

items.fix: Assert all nine copied fields on the update test (or switch update() to an @MappingTarget mapper so the compile guard covers it); at minimum add assertThat(updated.getPhone()).isEqualTo("+44 1738 111222"), plus countryCode, addressLine2 and county

items.fix: Rename the file to EmfMetricsPublisherAnnotationsTest.java and move it to src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/service/ alongside EmfMetricsPublisherTest, or fold the three reflection tests into EmfMetricsPublisherTest and delete this class

items.issue: No case covers a malformed JSON request body: HttpMessageNotReadableException extends RuntimeException, so GlobalExceptionHandler's @ExceptionHandler(RuntimeException.class) catch-all swallows it and returns 500 internal-error instead of a 400 bad-request problem - this missing case is exactly why that Critical shipped green
items.fix: Add malformedJsonBody_returns400BadRequestProblem: build a MockMvc standaloneSetup with a stub controller taking @RequestBody, POST content("{not json") with APPLICATION_JSON, and assert status 400, content type application/problem+json, $.type = https://api.cdp.defra.cloud/problems/bad-request and no $.errors key (the Problem, not ValidationProblem, branch) - it must fail until an @ExceptionHandler(HttpMessageNotReadableException.class) is added

items.fix: Drop the conditional and assert deterministically, e.g. assertThat(response.getBody().getProperties()).isNull(); (or isNullOrEmpty()), so the test actually pins the omit-traceId contract.

items.issue: handleTypeMismatch is the only one of the five handler methods in GlobalExceptionHandler with no unit test here; OperatorListIT.listWithANonNumericPageReturns400BadRequestProblem pins status/type/absent-errors but nothing pins the detail string "Invalid value for parameter '<name>'" that embeds ex.getName().
items.fix: Add a test calling exceptionHandler.handleTypeMismatch(new MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException("abc", Integer.class, "page", methodParameter, cause)) and assert the 400 bad-request type, the detail naming 'page', and doesNotContainKey("errors").

items.issue: The validationException helper builds its MethodParameter from getDeclaredMethod("setUp"), coupling all four validation tests to the name of an unrelated @BeforeEach lifecycle method; renaming setUp makes them fail with 'Failed to build MethodArgumentNotValidException', which points nowhere near the real cause.
items.fix: Reflect on a dedicated private placeholder (e.g. 'private void validationTarget(Object body) {}') declared next to the helper, so the reflected name exists only to serve the helper.

items.fix: Rename to handleValidationException_shouldReturn400WithCamelCaseErrorsMap etc. and add the Given/When/Then comment blocks.

items.issue: The no-PII-in-logs assertion is vacuous: IdentityHeaderFilter only logs inside reject(), so on this happy path appender.list is empty and allSatisfy() passes over zero events — the test would stay green if the filter logged the request body verbatim.

items.notes: Verified gone in refresh of IdentityHeaderFilter / IdentityHeaderFilterTest
