items.issue: None of the seven test methods use the mandated explicit // Given, // When, // Then comment blocks that every other unit test in the codebase follows.
items.fix: Add // Given, // When, // Then (or // When & Then for the short ones) to each test method.

items.issue: No test covers a DELETE racing a concurrent PUT (tombstone resurrection): Address has no @Version, so OperatorService.delete and update are both read-modify-write with a full-document repository.save(); a PUT that loaded the ACTIVE doc before the DELETE committed will save status=ACTIVE back over the tombstone and silently un-delete the address. Verified: no @Version, no ExecutorService/CountDownLatch anywhere in src/, so concurrency is untested in this IT and in the whole repo.
items.fix: Add an IT that interleaves the two read-modify-writes deterministically (load the entity, DELETE via mockMvc, then have the PUT save its stale copy) and assert the row stays DELETED; if it resurrects, add @Version to Address (or make delete/update partial @Query updates) so the losing write fails with OptimisticLockingFailureException.

items.issue: deleteCrossOrgIdReturns404AndLeavesAddressUntouched sends OTHER_ORG in BOTH the path and the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, so it only exercises the scoped-query miss, never the controller authoriseOrg guard (session-org != path orgId). AddressScopingIT.forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404 covers GET/list/PUT/POST but not DELETE, so deleting authoriseOrg(orgId, sessionOrg) from OperatorController.delete leaves every test in the repo green while allowing org B to soft-delete org A's address.
items.fix: Add a case with path=ORG and header=OTHER_ORG (and its mirror) asserting 404 plus the row still ACTIVE, or extend AddressScopingIT.forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404 with the DELETE verb.

items.issue: The only evidence that the second DELETE did not re-save is modifiedAt equality, and Mongo stores Instant at millisecond precision. If both DELETEs land within the same millisecond the assertion holds even with the early-return guard in OperatorService.delete removed, so the test can pass vacuously; it is a weak mutation detector for the very behaviour its name claims.
items.fix: Assert the write itself rather than its timestamp side effect - e.g. wrap OperatorRepository in a @SpyBean and verify(repository, times(1)).save(any()) across the two calls, or drive auditing from a controllable DateTimeProvider bean so the second save would produce a provably different modifiedAt.

items.issue: saveActive() sets .createdAt/.modifiedAt to a fixed Instant, but MongoConfig has @EnableMongoAuditing and Address carries @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate, so on save of a new (null-id) entity Spring Data overwrites both with now(). The two builder calls have no effect and mislead a reader into thinking the fixture's timestamps are the baseline the later modifiedAt assertions compare against.
items.fix: Drop the .createdAt/.modifiedAt builder calls and read the audited values back from the entity returned by repository.save() where a baseline is needed.

items.issue: Nothing asserts that a soft delete actually bumps modifiedAt and preserves createdAt, although both OperatorController.delete and OperatorService.delete document that modifiedAt is bumped on save. The unit test deleteFlipsAnActiveAddressToAdeletedTombstoneAndBumpsModifiedAt fakes the bump inside a mocked repository.save, so this IT is the only place real @LastModifiedDate auditing on the delete path can be proven - AddressUpdateIT.putBumpsModifiedAtAndPreservesCreatedAt does exactly this for PUT.
items.fix: In deleteLiveAddressReturns204AndKeepsRowWithDeletedStatus, capture the saved entity's createdAt/modifiedAt before the DELETE and assert modifiedAt isAfter the baseline and createdAt unchanged, mirroring AddressUpdateIT.putBumpsModifiedAtAndPreservesCreatedAt.

items.issue: Test methods do not follow the bundled IT convention {subject}_{shouldDoWhat}[_{whenContext}] (e.g. delete_shouldReturn204_whenAddressIsLive) and no test carries the mandated // Given, // When, // Then comment blocks; the doc states all ITs use them.
items.fix: Rename the five tests to the subject-prefixed form and add the Given/When/Then comment blocks, or - if this new repo is deliberately adopting a different convention - record that decision so the address-book best-practices bundle stops contradicting the code.

items.issue: Assertions pin camelCase wire names (jsonPath $.countryCode, $.organisationId, $.deleted) but the same PR commits docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml declaring snake_case (address_line_1, organisation_id, trace_id, country, telephone, status) — and docs/best-practices/rest-api/rest-api.md lists 'camelCase in JSON' under Don't. The compliance gate in OperatorComplianceIT only diffs path set, HTTP methods and operationIds against the locked contract, never schema properties, so this whole-model divergence ships untested. PR-wide issue, raised once here.
items.fix: Pick one authority: either regenerate/delete api-contract.locked.yaml so it matches the camelCase implementation, or move the implementation to snake_case; then extend the OperatorComplianceIT divergence gate to compare component schema property names, not just operationIds.

items.issue: getCrossOrgIdReturns404IdenticalToUnknownId is a near-verbatim duplicate of AddressScopingIT.a404ForAnotherOrgsLiveAddressIsByteIdenticalToA404ForAnUnknownId (same ORG_A/ORG_B/UNKNOWN_ID constants, same two requests, same problem-body equality) and assertThatProblemBodiesMatch duplicates AddressScopingIT.problemWithoutInstance. Both files are new in this PR, so the duplication is introduced here — two copies of a security-critical assertion will drift apart, and only one carries the comment explaining why instance is excluded.
items.fix: Delete the duplicate test from AddressGetIT and leave the cv-040 non-disclosure assertion in AddressScopingIT, which is the class that owns org scoping; or hoist the problem-body comparison helper into IntegrationBase and keep a single test.

items.issue: The happy-path GET asserts only 5 of the 14 OperatorResponse fields (id, name, countryCode, organisationId, deleted). The save() fixture seeds addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, phone, email, createdAt and modifiedAt but none is asserted, so an OperatorMapper regression that drops or mis-maps any of them — including addressLine1, the exact field the two committed contract documents disagree about — passes this IT green. For the endpoint the class javadoc frames as the GET contract test, that is the wrong half of the payload pinned.
items.fix: Assert the remaining mapped fields on getLiveAddressReturns200WithDeletedFalse (addressLine1, townOrCity, postcode, phone, email, and createdAt/modifiedAt as exists()), or compare the whole body against an expected JSON document with content().json(...).

items.issue: save() seeds createdAt and modifiedAt with fixed Instants, but Address carries @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate and MongoConfig enables @EnableMongoAuditing, so repository.save() overwrites both with the current clock on insert. The seeded 2026-07-14T09:15:27Z values never reach the database and are never asserted — dead fixture that implies deterministic timestamps the test does not have.
items.fix: Drop the createdAt/modifiedAt builder calls from save(), or assert the auditing behaviour explicitly (e.g. read the saved entity back and assert the timestamps are non-null and were set by auditing rather than by the fixture).

items.issue: The class javadoc claims cross-org and unknown ids yield 'byte-identical 404s (cv-040)', but assertThatProblemBodiesMatch deserialises both bodies into a Map and removes the instance key before comparing — so neither byte identity, key order, nor the Content-Type header is actually asserted, and instance legitimately differs. AddressScopingIT documents the instance exclusion inline; this copy states a stronger guarantee than its own assertion provides.
items.fix: Reword the javadoc to 'identical problem bodies apart from the RFC 9457 instance, which echoes the caller own request URI', matching the comment already written in AddressScopingIT.

items.issue: forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404 exercises the OperatorController.authoriseOrg mismatch guard for GET-by-id, list, PUT and POST but NOT DELETE - and no other test in the repo ever issues a DELETE where the path orgId differs from the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, so deleting authoriseOrg(orgId, sessionOrg) from OperatorController.delete would let org B soft-delete org A's address via A's path with the whole suite still green
items.fix: Add a DELETE leg to forwardedOrgHeaderDisagreeingWithThePathOrgIdIs404: perform delete(/organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{operator-id}, ORG_A, id).header(ORG_HEADER, ORG_B), expect 404, then assert the stored address is still AddressStatus.ACTIVE via repository.findById(id)

items.issue: problemWithoutInstance strips an 'instance' key that this service never emits - GlobalExceptionHandler builds ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail and never calls setInstance, and it does not extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, so instance is null and omitted; the comment at line 229-231 claiming instance echoes the request URI is wrong for this codebase and the exclusion pre-weakens the byte-identical assertion against a future change that does populate instance
items.fix: Drop problemWithoutInstance and compare the two parsed bodies directly, adding an explicit assertion that neither body contains an 'instance' key; if instance is later populated per-URI, reinstate the exclusion with a comment that matches the actual handler

items.issue: Cross-org exclusion is asserted on only ONE of the three search query paths: searchIsOrgScopedAndExcludesSoftDeleted (line 184) seeds OTHER_ORG and covers searchByQuery (q-only). countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code (122), combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode (153) and searchResultsPaginateAt25PreservingQueryAndCountryCode (222) seed ORG rows only, so deleting 'organisationId': ?0 from the raw @Query on searchByCountryCode or searchByQueryAndCountryCode leaves the whole suite green — org scoping in a @Query string is compiler-invisible and no other IT covers it (OperatorRepositoryIT only covers findByIdAndOrganisationId; OperatorServiceTest mocks the repository so it cannot see the query string).
items.fix: Seed an OTHER_ORG ACTIVE row that WOULD match in each of the two countryCode-path tests (e.g. an FR row for OTHER_ORG in countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code and in combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode) and assert jsonPath($.items[*].id, not(hasItem(otherOrg.getId()))) plus the exact totalItems, so all three repository query paths carry a cross-org guard.

items.issue: ACTIVE-only tombstone exclusion has the same one-path-of-three gap as the org guard. Only searchIsOrgScopedAndExcludesSoftDeleted (line 184) seeds a DELETED row, and it queries the q-only path. Neither countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code nor combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode seeds a tombstone, so losing the literal 'status': 'ACTIVE' from the searchByCountryCode or searchByQueryAndCountryCode @Query string would resurface soft-deleted addresses in country-filtered search results with no test failing.
items.fix: Seed an ORG-owned AddressStatus.DELETED row that matches the country filter in each countryCode-path test and assert it is absent — jsonPath($.items[*].id, not(hasItem(deleted.getId()))) and jsonPath($.items[*].deleted, everyItem(is(false))) — mirroring the assertions already used at lines 217-218.

items.issue: combinedQueryAndCountryCodeMatchesEitherTextOrCountryCode does not test what its name claims. It sends q=France + countryCode=FR, but no seeded row matches 'France' in name/townOrCity/postcode ('Paris Depot'/'Paris'/'75001' and 'London Depot'/'London'/'SW1A 1AA'), so only the countryCode arm of the $or in searchByQueryAndCountryCode is ever exercised — deleting the three regex clauses from that @Query leaves the test green, and the test is behaviourally identical to countryCodeParamMatchesStoredAlpha2Code above it. It also silently pins the (questionable) OR semantics whereby adding a countryCode WIDENS results rather than filtering them, without any row that proves the OR.
items.fix: Seed a third ORG row that matches by text only and NOT by country (e.g. name 'France Freight', countryCode 'GB'), then assert totalItems 2 and hasItem on both the text-only and the country-only ids. If the intended product behaviour is a filter (AND) rather than a widening (OR), confirm with the BA and change the @Query and this test together.

items.issue: searchResultsPaginateAt25PreservingQueryAndCountryCode asserts only page sizes (25 / 5) and counts, never that page 1 and page 2 are disjoint or that together they cover all 30 saved ids. The sort key is createdAt DESC only (OperatorService line 68) and is not unique: @EnableMongoAuditing + @CreatedDate stamp all 30 rows with Instant.now() at save time, persisted to Mongo at millisecond precision, so ties are expected. MongoDB skip/limit over a non-unique sort has no stable ordering, so a document can appear on both pages or on neither — the test would still pass, masking both a latent flake and a real pagination defect.
items.fix: Collect the 30 saved ids, read the id lists from both pages, and assert containsExactlyInAnyOrderElementsOf(allIds) on their union (and no intersection). If that goes red, add a unique tiebreaker to the sort in OperatorService — Sort.by(DESC, "createdAt").and(Sort.by(DESC, "id")) — and extend the org_status_created compound index accordingly.

items.issue: No test proves the search term is treated as a literal. OperatorService.toPartialMatchRegex wraps q in Pattern.quote (\\Q...\\E) precisely so a user-supplied regex metacharacter cannot become an operator — the ReDoS-safety claim in the OperatorRepository javadoc. That is compiler-invisible: replacing Pattern.quote(q.trim()) with q.trim() leaves every test in this file green, silently turning q into an attacker-controlled regex evaluated server-side against the whole org collection.
items.fix: Add a test that seeds e.g. 'Green Farm' and 'Blue Barn' and asserts q='.*' (or 'Gr(e)+n' / 'a+b') returns totalItems 0, and a positive case that a literal metacharacter in a stored value (e.g. postcode 'IV2 3JH' searched as 'V2 3') still matches — pinning that q is quoted, not compiled.

items.issue: The save() helper sets .createdAt(Instant.parse("2026-07-14T09:15:27Z")) and .modifiedAt(...) on every seeded Address, but Address.createdAt/modifiedAt carry @CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate and MongoConfig has @EnableMongoAuditing, so Spring Data's auditing handler overwrites both with Instant.now() on insert. The two builder lines have no effect and mislead a reader into thinking the test controls the createdAt sort key used by the newest-first pagination.
items.fix: Drop the two timestamp builder calls, or — if a controlled sort key is actually wanted (see the pagination finding) — set createdAt to distinct values via repository/MongoTemplate after save so the ordering under test is deterministic.

items.issue: putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals asserts only 4 of the 9 fields OperatorService.update() hand-copies (name, addressLine1, townOrCity, countryCode); postcode, phone and email are never asserted on the PUT path here, and phone is asserted nowhere in the whole suite on the update path (OperatorServiceTest lines 178-182 cover postcode/email but not phone), so deleting existing.setPhone(request.phone()) from OperatorService.update() passes every test
items.fix: Add jsonPath assertions for $.postcode, $.phone and $.email to the 200 response chain and to the repository.findById satisfies() block, so all nine hand-copied setters are covered

items.issue: No test covers concurrent access to PUT: Address has no @Version field, so OperatorService.update() is an unguarded read-modify-write (findByIdAndOrganisationId then repository.save of the whole document). Two overlapping PUTs silently lose one writer's fields, and a DELETE landing between the update read and its save resurrects the tombstone back to ACTIVE - neither path is exercised here or anywhere in the repo (no @Execution parallel, no CountDownLatch/ExecutorService test)
items.fix: Add an IT that runs two overlapping PUTs (and a PUT interleaved with a DELETE) via an ExecutorService against the shared Mongo container and asserts the intended outcome; if last-write-wins and tombstone resurrection are accepted, encode that as an explicit documented test, otherwise add @Version to Address and assert the 409/retry

items.issue: Three of the five tests duplicate PUT tests added by the same PR in OperatorCrudIT: putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals overlaps putReplacesTheMutableFieldsReturns200AndBumpsModifiedAt (line 327) plus putClearsAnOmittedOptionalFieldBecauseItIsAFullReplace (line 358); putBumpsModifiedAtAndPreservesCreatedAt re-covers the same modifiedAt bump; putOnSoftDeletedTombstoneReturns404 duplicates putOnADeletedTombstoneReturns404 (line 377) but asserts strictly less (no Content-Type, no status, no errors-absent check) - two ITs must now be kept in step for one endpoint
